transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You have that look. Like you think you can still go back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Where is my brother, old man. I've been calling his name till it hurt.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice. I don't like being heard, and they like it even less. You came in hot like the valley still answers you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't care who hears me. Omar came this way.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I flinch because noise gets remembered here. Don't take it personal. I see the same pull in you I saw in others, and it never ends well.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stop circling me. Did you see him or not.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I don't track faces anymore, boy, I lose them if I try. Names slip first, then eyes, then you're left with shapes. Tell me why you're shaking if you're so sure.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I'm tired, not scared. Why are you still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Trapped, if you want the clean word. It sounds worse than it feels; this fountain is the only place that hasn't killed me yet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Forty years hiding. That's not wisdom.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I never said it was. It's just what keeps the stones from noticing you breathe. If you want clever, ask someone who's dead.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who's watching us right now.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The houses. Not the walls, what leans behind them. They measure themselves by how close they dare stand to this oil.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Where would they take someone like Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Not far from here, not where you can point. Being taken isn't moving; it's being kept. If he was only lost, the oil would have finished him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What crawls in the oil.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The pale hands are what's left of people who bargained wrong. They aren't jinn, and they don't think anymore. I won't look at them when they rise, and neither should you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Who keeps him, then. Say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower — just listen. Everything here answers to a king, whether it wants to or not, and that is why your brother is kept. His daughter stands at the gate; she doesn't ask questions, she reads what you carry and waits to see if it breaks you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there anything that actually works against this dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't ask that so loud. There is light that makes the oil pull back and the watchers go quiet, just long enough to move. Knowing it is safer than using it, and I've lived by that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then give it to me. The prayer.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: No. Saying it costs, and the cost isn't quick. I've stayed alive by never ringing a bell here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why didn't you use it to get free.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I chose the fear I could live with. That's all there is.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then what was that silence just now.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: It was me realizing you aren't running. That doesn't make you safe, it just makes my reasons sound small, and I hate that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not backing off.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The hands are the first problem; they reach before anything else does. The prayer pushes them down, but it rings like a bell, and bells get remembered. I will give it, but let the square settle first or it will take more than you're offering.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stop stalling. Give it now.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There's a gap that opens after the first word, and things listen inside it. If your fear spikes there, the oil takes a piece you won't notice until it's gone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Look at me and say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The bubbling slowed; that's worse, not better. When it goes quiet, it's deciding who to mark. Don't push closer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then say it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the hands touch you — not before. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: When do I use it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Only when the hands reach you. If you pull it early, the oil learns your shape faster.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Stay strong.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I don't know how to answer that, but hearing it matters. You're doing what I never did, and that counts.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Repeat the one thing I must not forget.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use it only when the hands touch you, and keep your fear from spiking in the gap. I hope you find a better end than mine.
